name: Legislative/Lobby Committee Liaison Meeting Agenda
minutes_text:
CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 North Rexford Drive
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210
  Video Teleconference
  Beverly Hills City Council Liaison / Legislative / Lobby Committee Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Friday, May 24, 2024
  10:30 AM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  May 24, 2024 / 10:30 AM
IN ATTENDANCE:  Vice Mayor Sharona Nazarian, Councilmember John Mirisch, Deputy City
  Manager Keith Sterling, Municipal Affairs Program Manager Cynthia
  Owens, City Attorney Lawrence Weiner, Police Captain Elisabeth
  Albanese

  A. Oral Communications:
  a. Sherwin Shamoeli, Senior Field Representative for the Office of Rick Chavez: He
  stated that AB 2943 passed the State Assembly and gave an overview of what the
  bill is, and then introduced the retail crime bipartisan bill package. He concluded
  by stating his availability should the committee have any questions about the bill.

  B. Direction:
  1. S.2632 - Visa Processing Improvement Act
  i. Councilmember Mirisch is opposed to the bill because it covers all nations,
  and does not exclude Qatar.
  ii. The Liaisons would support if amended to exclude countries that are
  supportive of terrorists such as Qatar.
  2. Retail Theft Legislation – Over Sixteen bills are moving through the Legislature
  that will make meaningful statutory changes to address the increase in retail theft.
  Below are the main bills the League of California Cities is either supporting or
  supporting if amended. Staff is seeking direction from the Legislative / Lobby
  Liaisons on the following state legislative bills:
  A. Assembly Bill 2943 (Zbur) - Crimes: shoplifting
  i. The Police department supports all the bills in the Retail Theft
  Legislation List.
  ii. The League of California Cities supports this bill if amended to
  include provisions in the aggregations section of the bill to include
  the rules as set forth in People v Bailey for cases relating to multiple
  thefts. They also want to amend the ability to arrest section to include
  the ability for police to use unsworn statements taken from one or
  more persons when these statements demonstrate probable cause.
  Their last amendment is that completion of probation should be
  determined by the probation supervising court.
  iii. Both Liaison support the bill as is but would like if the bill was
  amended to include the League’s suggestions.
 Highlights for May 24, 2024
Legislative / Lobby Committee

  B. Assembly Bill 1960 (Soria) - Sentencing enhancements: property loss.
  i. The League of California Cities fully supports this bill.
  ii. Both Liaison support the bill.
  C. Assembly Bill 3209 (Berman) - Crimes: theft: retail theft restraining orders
  i. The League of California Cities fully supports this bill.
  ii. Both Liaison support the bill.
  D. Senate Bill 1242 (Min) - Crimes: fires
  i. The League of California Cities fully supports this bill.
  ii. Both Liaison support the bill.

  i. The League of California Cities fully supports this bill.
  ii. Both Liaison support the bill.

  i. The League of California Cities fully supports this bill.
  ii. Both Liaison support the bill.
  G. Senate Bill 982 (Wahab) - Crimes: organized theft
  i. The League of California Cities fully supports this bill.
  ii. Both Liaison support the bill.
  H. Assembly Bill 1779 (Irwin) - Theft: jurisdiction

  I. Assembly Bill 1794 (McCarty) - Crimes: larceny

  J. Senate Bill 1144 (Skinner) - Marketplaces: online marketplaces

  K. Senate Bill 1381 (McGuire) Property crimes: regional property crimes task

  i. The League of California Cities fully supports this bill.

  L. Senate Bill 1416 (Newman) - Sentencing enhancements: sale, exchange,

  i. The League of California Cities fully supports this bill.
  ii. Both Liaison support the bill.
  M. Assembly Bill 1990 (Carrillo, Wendy) - Criminal procedure: arrests:
  shoplifting
  i. The League of California Cities fully support this bill
  ii. Both Liaison support the bill.
  3.  Senate Bill 926 (Wahab) - Crimes: distribution of intimate images
  i. Both Liaison support the bill.
  4.  Assembly Bill 2309 (Muratsuchi) - City attorney: state law: misdemeanor
  i. The City Attorney is in support of this bill.
  ii. Both Liaison support the bill.
  5.  Senate Bill 1262 (Archuleta) - Crimes: supervised release

  ii. PD supports the bill.
  6.  Senate Bill 1180 (Ashby) - Health care coverage: emergency medical services
  i. Both Liaison support the bill
  7.  Assembly Bill 2584 (Lee) - Single-family residential real property: corporate entity:

Legislative / Lobby Committee

  i. Both Liaison support the bill.
  8. Ballot Initiative (22-0008) ? Expands Local Governments? Authority to Enact Rent
  Control on Residential Property.
  i. Councilmember Mirisch is in support however Vice Mayor Nazarian wants
  to hold off her decision until next time so she can get a better understanding

  9. Senate Bill 1116 (Portantino) - Unemployment insurance: trade disputes: eligibility

  13. Legislative Updates
  i. Ted Lieu has requested an earmark $2 million for replacing 3 miles of water

  ii. Congress reenacted the FAA.

  i. None
